intro: CSV to Table renders raw CSV text as a clean, column-aligned monospace table so you can read it without a spreadsheet. It pads each column to a consistent width, separates cells with a pipe character, and adds a divider line under the first row to mark it as a header. This is handy whenever you paste CSV from a log, an export, or an API response and just want to view and align the data quickly.
useCases: Quickly inspecting a CSV export or log snippet without opening Excel or Google Sheets
Aligning messy comma-separated data into readable columns before pasting it into a ticket or chat
Eyeballing whether rows have a consistent number of columns
Reviewing CSV pulled from an API response or database dump
Pasting CSV into documentation or a code comment as a fixed-width ASCII table

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The tool runs entirely in your browser and parses the CSV locally. Nothing you paste is uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere.
Yes. Parsing is handled by PapaParse, which detects the delimiter automatically, so comma, semicolon, and tab-separated values all work without configuration.

faq.q: Is the first row treated as a header?
faq.a: Visually, yes. The first row is rendered like the others, but a divider line is inserted directly beneath it to set it apart as a header.

faq.q: What happens to empty lines or missing cells?
faq.a: Empty lines are skipped during parsing. Rows with fewer columns than the widest row are padded with blanks so every column stays aligned.

faq.q: Why do I get an error instead of a table?
faq.a: If the input has no rows after trimming and skipping empty lines, you will see a "No data to render" message. Fatal parse errors from malformed CSV are also reported instead of producing partial output.
